strengths: Novel and well-motivated KL divergence perspective that provides genuine new insights into Shampoo's second-moment estimation and its limitations
Solid mathematical framework with rigorous proofs of three main claims connecting KL minimization to covariance estimation
Practical contribution of eliminating Adam grafting requirement, reducing memory overhead while maintaining stability
Natural extension to tensor-valued weights without requiring additional modifications
Clear presentation with good motivation for why KL divergence is more appropriate than Frobenius norm for SPD-constrained optimization
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental validation: all results labeled 'preliminary,' no statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or error bars; random search with 120 runs is insufficient methodology for top-tier venues
Marginal practical improvements: Figure 2 shows KL-Shampoo meeting or only slightly exceeding SOAP's efficiency; improvements are visually small and don't strongly justify adoption of new method
Extremely restricted experimental scope: only language model pretraining on 4 models (123-227M), single set of datasets; no evaluation on vision, RL, or other domains where Shampoo is used
Missing critical ablation studies on key design choices: moving average scheme for eigenvalues, damping parameter κ, QR decomposition frequency, and impact of eigenbasis staleness

Inadequately addressed theory-practice gap: Claim 2's circular dependency between S*_a and S*_b resolved by approximation (Eq. 4), but this approximation lacks rigorous justification and convergence analysis
Missing implementation details: damping parameter κ introduced but never discussed for selection; hyperparameter ranges for random search not specified; no code availability mentioned
Incomplete analysis of results: no explanation for why Shampoo (p=1/2) completely fails on RWKV7 without grafting, or why Shampoo (p=1/4, graft) outperforms KL-Shampoo on some runs
Tensor extension insufficiently validated: claims 'natural extension' but only tests on single model (NanoMoE) with no ablation comparing tensor vs. vectorized formulations

Limited baseline comparisons: missing comparisons with standard optimizers (Adam, SGD) for context, other recent second-order methods, and recent Shampoo variants cited heavily (Morwani 2025, Eschenhagen 2025, An 2025, Xie 2025)
No computational analysis: lacks wall-clock time comparisons, FLOPs analysis, or detailed memory savings quantification despite claiming memory benefits

strengths: Novel KL divergence perspective for understanding Shampoo/SOAP that naturally respects SPD constraints and extends to tensor-valued weights; well-grounded in information geometry and quasi-Newton theory
Solid theoretical contributions (Claims 1-7) with clear proofs characterizing optimal covariance estimators; Claim 3 provides proximal-gradient interpretation of EMA schemes

Practical algorithm design: efficient QR-based implementation with clever EMA scheme for eigenvalue estimation using outdated eigenbasis; achieves SOAP-level runtime while eliminating Adam memory overhead

Comprehensive empirical validation: extensive hyperparameter search (150 runs per method), consistent improvements across 4 LM architectures, thorough comparisons with F-Shampoo and VN-Shampoo variants demonstrating KL advantages
Clear presentation with well-motivated introduction and effective use of figures; implementation details support reproducibility; broader applicability shown by improving multiple Shampoo variants
weaknesses: No convergence analysis or theoretical guarantees for proposed algorithms; gap between idealized updates (exact expectations) and stochastic versions not addressed; no formal analysis of EMA approximation error accumulation

Limited experimental scope: only language model pretraining domain tested; models are small (123M-227M params); only 1-2.5B tokens; unclear if improvements scale to modern large models (10B+); no statistical significance testing despite visible variance in results (Fig. 5)

Unexplained key phenomenon: 'Surprisingly, KL-Shampoo outperforms KL-SOAP' contradicts the two-sided optimality narrative and deserves deeper investigation; why do augmented full-diagonal eigenvalues underperform Kronecker-factored eigenvalues?

Implementation bias concerns: different implementations for different methods (official SOAP vs. authors' Shampoo implementation); no ablation studies isolating contributions of QR vs. EMA vs. two-sided structure; no wall-clock time measurements despite SOAP-level runtime claims

Gap between theory and practice: block-diagonal Hessian choice in Claim 3 is mathematically convenient but not deeply justified; tight connection to matrix Gaussian theory and Lin et al. (2019) suggests ideas partially known; missing comparisons with other structured methods beyond Shampoo variants

Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance testing; improvements over SOAP often modest (2-5%); sensitivity analysis lacking for key hyperparameters (β₂, decomposition frequency, damping); practical memory improvements over SOAP not quantified on actual runs

strengths: Novel and well-motivated KL divergence perspective on second-moment estimation that respects SPD constraint, with clear theoretical justification
Rigorous theoretical contributions with five formal claims and complete proofs characterizing optimal solutions for covariance estimation
Comprehensive empirical evaluation with 150 random search runs per method across multiple architectures (GPT, RWKV, Llama, MoE), reducing variance and enabling robust comparisons
Practical algorithmic innovations including EMA scheme for eigenvalue estimation with outdated eigenbasis and QR integration, achieving SOAP-level runtime
Memory efficiency gains by eliminating Adam overhead and competitive performance without step-size grafting
Clean distinction between idealized theoretical schemes and practical implementations with systematic ablations (e.g., Fig. 4 on EMA vs. instantaneous eigenvalues)
Natural extension to tensor-valued weights demonstrated empirically, showing framework generality
weaknesses: Empirical scope limited to language model pretraining on relatively small models (123M-227M); no evaluation on vision, other NLP tasks, or different domains
Modest practical improvements over SOAP (1-3% on test loss); unclear if benefits persist at 10B+ scale or different optimization regimes
Theoretical gaps: no convergence analysis for practical EMA scheme; gap between idealized Eq. (4) and practical Eq. (5) not formally analyzed; no convergence rates
Confounded comparisons especially in Fig. 5: all methods benefit from QR+EMA engineering improvements, making it difficult to isolate pure effect of KL divergence choice
Surprising result that KL-Shampoo outperforms KL-SOAP lacks explanation—intuition for why removing Adam in eigenbasis improves optimization is missing
Baseline implementation inconsistencies: SOAP uses official implementation while KL-methods use authors' implementation; unclear if this affects results
Missing ablations on damping parameter κ, QR update frequency sensitivity, and β₂ parameter effects; limited analysis of which design choices drive performance
Reproducibility concerns: code not provided, some implementation details underspecified (e.g., precision handling), hyperparameter search distributions not fully specified
No end-to-end wall-clock training time comparisons; experiments limited to ~150-300 minutes, unclear if improvements hold over full training
Limited novelty of practical techniques: QR decomposition from SOAP (Vyas et al. 2025a); EMA scheme is standard technique applied in new context
